brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
The black tea made under Tianfu Longya, a Sichuan geographical indication covering the mountains rimming the Sichuan basin and the hills within it.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
name_ru: Тянь Фу Лун Я Хун Ча
history: Tianfu Longya counts among the ten famous teas of Sichuan, and in 2015 it received a Golden Camel award for Chinese famous teas at a centennial Expo commemoration. Little is documented about the black tea on its own.
processing: Typical of black tea: withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: Picked through the growing season, as with most black teas.
appearance_dry: Fine, tight strips with visible golden tips.
taste_profile: Mellow and clean, with an aroma of tangerine and candied sugar.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
